feat(tokens): measure what a reader loads, counted rather than estimated (S38, ADR-064)

Review 0002 S38 filed the estate's always-on context at 90 KB per turn, 72% of
it a paragraph an earlier root had already loaded. It arrived as a hand count
over seven repositories, which ages with the first rule edit and cannot be
re-derived by the reader who has to act on it. This is that reading, as a
command: bytes per channel, an approximate token figure, and -- across a
workspace -- every repeated paragraph attributed to the first root that carries
it, by the same byte-exact blank-line method the review used, in sorted path
order so the figure is reproducible.

Three choices keep the number defensible, and each is a ruling rather than a
default: the budget being defended is the projection's, so hand-written bytes
are reported beside it and not folded in; a region is the span between its two
markers, so the blank line a person left above the marker is billed to nobody;
and an over-budget repository is reported rather than failed, because a meter
that went red would train people to ignore the figure it exists to print.

The flag is --repos rather than the plan's --workspace, which has been a value
flag since plan 0002 naming a directory of skill sources. One flag with two
meanings is the silent-ignore defect the argument parser refuses.

readLimitFindings now returns the reader, the limit, the byte offset and the
overage beside its prose, so the meter and the check that already reported the
Codex limit read the same numbers instead of each re-deriving them.

S38 stays open: this is the instrument. The 30 KB figure needs R07's kernel,
R08's per-repository budget field, R11's dedupe and the R01-R05 evaluation of
moving process rules behind skills.
